Laura — thanks for the clear list. Below are concise commitments we can put into the DPA and ops playbook for the pilot. I attached a proposed redline and an ops evidence pack stub for initial review.

1) Model improvement opt-out: confirmed. For Navexa pilot traffic we will tag the tenant as "model_improvement_excluded" and route to a non-adaptive serving path. This will prevent training/aggregation for model updates. We will include the exact language in the DPA clause ("we will not use customer content to train or improve models").

2) Subprocessor notifications: we maintain a current subprocessors list in our portal and will send 30 days' notice by email for any additions that affect Navexa's data. For the pilot we will limit processing to Redwood-managed US regions (no cross-border compute). If an emergency requires cross-border fallback, we'll notify and require explicit written approval.

3) Output ownership: Redwood grants customers a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free right to use, reproduce, and display outputs. We do not claim ownership over customer outputs. We'll add an explicit OS clause in the DPA acknowledging Navexa's product use case and permitting customer sublicensing to end users.

4) Evidence pack / ops contact: assigned ops lead is Marissa Cole (marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com). Initial evidence attached: ops-evidence-pack.pdf (high level items: data residency options, audit-log sample, SFTP export acceptance test) and sftp-instructions.txt with export flow. For procurement timing, we aim to deliver a full evidence bundle by 9/10.
